body: Your SB1 Bank account will be BLOCKED in 2 hours. Update KYC now: https://sb1-kyc-update.example/verify
explanation: Real banks do not threaten to block an account within two hours over SMS, and they never send a KYC link. The domain sb1-kyc-update.example imitates a bank name but is not the bank's own address.
lesson: A deadline measured in hours plus a link is the classic pressure combination. Open your bank app directly instead of tapping any link.

subject: Payment failed - account suspended
body:
Dear Customer,

We could not process your last payment. Your account has been suspended. To restore service within 24 hours, confirm your card details here:

https://netfliix-billing.invalid/restore

Regards,
Billing Team
explanation: "Dear Customer" instead of your name, a doubled letter in the sender domain (netfliix), and a request to re-enter card details on a linked page. Any one of these is suspicious; all three together is a template.
lesson: A service you pay for already has your name and your card. Being asked to re-enter them through a link is the tell.

body: Congratulations! You have won Rs 25,00,000 in the RBI Lucky Draw. Send your Aadhaar photo and bank passbook to claim. Pay only Rs 500 processing fee. Reply within today!
explanation: The RBI does not run lucky draws. An unsaved number asking for Aadhaar and passbook images plus an upfront fee is an advance-fee scam.
lesson: If you must pay money to receive money, it is a scam. Government bodies never ask for documents over WhatsApp.

subject: URGENT: Re-verify your student login
body:
Dear Student,

Our records show your portal credentials have expired. Re-verify using your enrolment number and current password within 12 hours or your account will be deactivated.

Verify: http://college-portal-verify.example/login

- Administration
explanation: It asks for your current password on a page reached from a link, addresses you as "Dear Student", and the domain merely contains the words college-portal.
lesson: Your college will never ask for your password by email. Type the portal address yourself or use the bookmark you already have.

body: AMZON: Delivery failed due to incomplete address. Update in 4 hrs to avoid return: amzn-redeliver.example/addr . Reply STOP to opt out.
explanation: The sender ID is misspelled (AMZON), the domain is not amazon.in, and the opt-out line is genuine-looking dressing added to make the message feel routine.
lesson: A plausible-looking footer does not validate the message above it. Check the sender spelling and the actual domain, not the tone.

body: Forwarded many times: *TCS is hiring 500 freshers, no interview!* Apply before tonight with your 10th marksheet and a Rs 1,200 registration fee. Link: tcs-campus-drive.invalid/apply
explanation: "No interview" plus an upfront registration fee is the giveaway. Legitimate campus drives never charge candidates, and a message forwarded many times carries no authority.
lesson: Forward counts are not verification. If a job requires you to pay to apply, the job is the product.

subject: Refund of Rs 4,999 initiated - action required
body:
Hi,

A merchant has initiated a refund of Rs 4,999 to your UPI ID. To credit it we need you to approve a COLLECT request on your UPI app within 30 minutes, or the refund lapses.

Approve using the collect ID in the attached file.

Thanks,
Refund Desk
explanation: This inverts the usual scam: it offers money rather than demanding it. But a genuine UPI refund needs nothing from you, and approving a COLLECT request moves money OUT of your account. The attachment hides the real collect ID.
lesson: Receiving money never requires you to approve a request. Any UPI prompt you did not initiate is a withdrawal, whatever the message calls it.

subject: Free laptop scheme - final day
body:
GOVT FREE LAPTOP SCHEME - FINAL DAY
Scan the QR and enter your Aadhaar number plus the OTP sent to your phone to confirm slot booking. Limited slots. Students who miss today lose the scheme benefit permanently.
explanation: A physical flyer feels more trustworthy than an email, which is exactly why it works. But it asks for an Aadhaar number and a live OTP, and an OTP is never a booking confirmation - it is the second factor for something already in progress.
lesson: Offline media can carry online scams. Never read an OTP aloud or type it into a form; an OTP completes a transaction someone else started.

subject: Library book due on 22 November
body:
Hello Ananya,

This is a reminder that "Introduction to Algorithms" is due back on 22 November. You can renew it twice from your library account.

No action is needed if you have already returned it.

- Central Library
explanation: It uses your name, comes from the college's own domain, asks for nothing, contains no link and no deadline threat. It even tells you that doing nothing is fine.
lesson: A legitimate notice asks you to do something you can already do through a channel you already have. Absence of a link is a strong positive signal.

body: SBI: Rs 5,000 debited from A/c XX4471 on 18-11 to UPI/1234. If this was not you, call 1800-11-2211 or report in the YONO app. Do not share OTP/PIN.
explanation: A real transaction alert names the official helpline, tells you to use the app you already have, and explicitly warns you not to share an OTP or PIN. It asks for no credentials and contains no link.
lesson: Genuine bank alerts direct you to channels you already trust and warn you against sharing secrets. Scams do the opposite.

body: Beta, your uncle's flight lands at 6:40pm. Papa will pick him up, you don't need to come. Dinner at 9. Call me if you're free after class.
explanation: A saved contact, ordinary family logistics, no link, no request for money or credentials, and no urgency beyond normal planning.
lesson: Most messages you receive are harmless. Treating everything as suspicious is as useless as treating nothing as suspicious - the skill is telling them apart.

subject: [phishtap-lite] Priya commented on your pull request #14
body:
Priya left a comment on your pull request:

"The ring buffer eviction looks right, but can you add a test for the case where ack runs past newest?"

You are receiving this because you authored the thread.

View it on GitHub: https://github.com/notifications

Unsubscribe: https://github.com/settings/notifications
explanation: This one is hard because it has a link, an automated sender and a generic-looking footer - all things that also appear in phishing. What makes it legitimate is that the link points to the real domain, the content references something you actually did, and it asks for no credentials.
lesson: The presence of a link is not evidence of phishing. Check where the link points and whether the message asks you to authenticate.

body: Your electricity bill for consumer 4471882 is Rs 1,240, due 25-11. Pay in your usual app or at any counter. Ignore if already paid. Helpline 1912.
explanation: It states your actual consumer number, gives the official 1912 helpline, tells you to use your usual app rather than a link, and says to ignore it if already paid. There is no link and no threat.
lesson: A real utility reminder gives you a reference number you can check independently and never routes you through a link.

subject: NSS camp registration - 20 to 24 December
body:
NSS SPECIAL CAMP, 20-24 DEC
Village: Rampur. Registration open till 5 December at the NSS office, Room 12, Admin Block.
Carry your college ID. No fee. Limited to 40 volunteers; the list will be posted on the same board on 8 December.

- Programme Officer, NSS
explanation: Registration happens in person at a named room, there is no fee, no QR code, no OTP and no link. The deadline is a real administrative date, not a countdown designed to stop you thinking.
lesson: Legitimate offline processes stay offline. A poster that routes you to a phone form is doing something a notice board has no reason to do.

subject: Semester 5 exam timetable published
body:
Dear students,

The Semester 5 examination timetable is now published on the college website under Examinations > Timetable.

Students with a clash between two papers should report to the examination cell with their hall ticket before 30 November.

- Office of the Registrar
explanation: It points you to a section of the website you already know, names a physical office for the one case that needs action, and attaches nothing. No credentials are requested.
lesson: Institutional announcements describe where information is; they do not send you to fetch it through an unfamiliar link.

body:
Rohit: does anyone have the notes for today's DBMS lecture?
Sana: I have them, will share to the drive folder after dinner.
You: thanks Sana
Rohit: also the assignment is due Friday, Prof mentioned it in class
explanation: An ordinary group conversation between people you know, with no link, no request for money or credentials, and no urgency beyond a normal assignment deadline that was also announced in class.
lesson: Context you can verify independently - a deadline your professor stated in person - is the strongest signal a message is genuine.

subject: Job Offer: Software Engineer at TCS - Immediate Joining
body:
Dear Candidate,

Congratulations! You have been selected for the position of Software Engineer at TCS with a package of Rs 8,50,000 per year.

To accept this offer, please pay Rs 2,500 as document verification fee within 24 hours:

Payment link: https://tcs-recruitment.example/pay

After payment, you will receive your offer letter.

Regards,
HR Department
TCS
explanation: No company asks you to pay to accept a job offer. The domain is not tcs.com, and legitimate recruitment never requires an upfront fee. The 24-hour deadline is designed to stop you from checking.
lesson: If a job requires you to pay to get it, the job is the product. Real companies pay you, not the other way around.

body: IRCTC: Your PNR 8547221099 is WAITLISTED. Confirm ticket by paying Rs 250 within 1 hr: irctc-confirm.example/pay . Else ticket will be cancelled.
explanation: IRCTC never asks you to pay to confirm a waitlisted ticket - that happens automatically. The domain is not irctc.co.in, and the one-hour deadline is pressure to act without thinking.
lesson: Waitlist confirmation is automatic and free. Any message asking you to pay to keep a reservation is a scam.

body: Namaste! I am from Amazon Customer Care. Your order #402-8874521-9988744 has been delivered but payment is pending. Please pay Rs 1,299 to avoid legal action. UPI ID: amazon-refund@okhdfcbank
explanation: Amazon never contacts you from an unsaved number, and a delivered order cannot have pending payment. The UPI ID is fake - amazon-refund@okhdfcbank is not an official Amazon account. The threat of legal action is intimidation.
lesson: Official customer care contacts you through the app or website, never from a random WhatsApp number. Threats of legal action over a small amount are always fake.

subject: Security alert: New sign-in from Windows device
body:
Hi,

We noticed a new sign-in to your Google Account from a Windows device in Mumbai, India.

If this was you, no action is needed.

If you don't recognize this activity, secure your account immediately:
https://googIe-accounts.example/security-check

This link expires in 12 hours for your protection.

Thanks,
The Google Accounts team
explanation: The domain uses a capital I instead of a lowercase l (googIe vs google), which is hard to spot. Real Google security alerts come from accounts-noreply@google.com and link to accounts.google.com. The 12-hour expiry is pressure.
lesson: Lookalike domains use similar characters (I for l, 0 for O). Always check the actual domain in the address bar, not the sender name.

body: HDFC Bank: Your debit card will be BLOCKED today. Update KYC to continue services: hdfc-kyc-update.example/verify . Call 1800-202-6161 for help.
explanation: The helpline number is real (which makes it look legitimate), but the link is not hdfcbank.com. Banks never send KYC update links via SMS. The word BLOCKED in caps is designed to panic you.
lesson: A real helpline number does not validate a fake link. Banks communicate KYC requirements through official letters or the app, never SMS links.

body:
Forwarded many times: 🎓 *PM Vidyalakshmi Scholarship 2024* 🎓

All students with 60%+ marks eligible. Amount: Rs 50,000 per year.

Last date: 30 November (extended from 15 Nov)

Apply now: pmvs-scholarship.example/apply

Required: Aadhaar, bank passbook, 10th marksheet

Share with all students! 🙏
explanation: The forward count suggests popularity but not legitimacy. The domain is not a .gov.in address, it asks for sensitive documents, and the extended deadline is a classic pressure tactic. Real government schemes are announced through official channels.
lesson: Forward counts are not verification. Government scholarships are announced on .gov.in websites and through colleges, not WhatsApp forwards.

subject: WiFi password change - action required
body:
ATTENTION HOSTEL RESIDENTS

The WiFi password has been changed for security reasons.

To get the new password:
1. Scan the QR code below
2. Enter your room number and current WiFi password
3. You will receive the new password via SMS

Do this before 10 PM today or your internet will be disconnected.

- Hostel Administration
explanation: A real password change would be announced in person or through the hostel warden. Asking for your current password to get a new one is backwards - it's harvesting credentials. The QR code routes you to a fake login page.
lesson: Password changes are communicated through the channel you already use, not through a new QR code. Never enter your current password to get a new one.

subject: Your Spotify Premium trial is ending - 3 months free!
body:
Hi there,

Your free trial of Spotify Premium ends in 48 hours.

Good news! We're offering you 3 months of Premium for FREE as a valued user.

Claim your offer: https://spotify-premium-offer.example/claim

You'll need to enter your payment details to verify your account, but you won't be charged for 3 months.

Enjoy the music!
The Spotify Team
explanation: The domain is not spotify.com, and asking for payment details to get something free is a contradiction. Real free trials don't require payment verification. The 48-hour deadline is pressure.
lesson: If you have to enter payment details to get something free, it's not free. Check the domain - spotify.com, not spotify-something.example.

body: Flipkart Big Billion Days: You've won a Rs 10,000 gift card! Claim now: flipkart-rewards.example/claim . Valid for 24 hrs only. T&C apply.
explanation: Flipkart doesn't give away gift cards via SMS to random numbers. The domain is not flipkart.com, and the 24-hour validity is pressure. The sender ID FLIPKART can be spoofed.
lesson: You can't win a contest you didn't enter. Retailers announce offers through their app and website, not unsolicited SMS.

body:
Hello, this is Rajesh Kumar, Branch Manager, SBI Main Branch.

Your account has been flagged for suspicious activity. To avoid freezing, please verify your identity by sending:
1. Aadhaar photo
2. PAN card photo
3. Last 4 digits of debit card
4. OTP you will receive

Send these on WhatsApp immediately. This is confidential.
explanation: A real bank manager would never ask for documents over WhatsApp from an unsaved number. Asking for an OTP is the biggest red flag - it's the second factor for a transaction already in progress. The confidentiality claim is to prevent you from asking others.
lesson: Banks never ask for OTPs or documents over WhatsApp. If someone claims to be from your bank, hang up and call the official number.

subject: Action Required: Update your academic profile
body:
Dear Student,

As per UGC guidelines, all students must update their academic profiles with Aadhaar and bank details for scholarship disbursement.

Please update your profile within 7 days:
https://yourcollege-ac-portal.example/update

Failure to update will result in scholarship cancellation.

Regards,
Academic Section
Your College
explanation: The domain is not your college's official domain. UGC guidelines don't require Aadhaar updates via email links. The threat of scholarship cancellation is pressure. Real administrative requests come through the official portal you already use.
lesson: Official college communications come from the college's own domain. Check the sender address, not just the signature.

subject: Part-time job opportunity for students
body:
EARN RS 15,000/MONTH - PART TIME

Work from hostel, 2 hours/day
No experience needed

Tasks: Data entry, form filling

Registration fee: Rs 500 (refundable after 1 month)

Scan QR to register
Slots limited - register today!

Contact: 98XXX XXX78 (WhatsApp only)
explanation: A refundable registration fee is never refundable. The high pay for minimal work is unrealistic. WhatsApp-only contact means no paper trail. The QR code leads to a form that harvests personal data and payment.
lesson: If a job requires you to pay to start, it's a scam. Legitimate part-time jobs are advertised through the college placement cell.

subject: [phishtap-lite] New issue assigned to you
body:
You were assigned to issue #42:

"Add corpus validation script"

View it on GitHub: https://github.com/priyanshu2119/phishtap-lite/issues/42

You are receiving this because you were assigned.
Unsubscribe: https://github.com/settings/notifications
explanation: This is a real GitHub notification. The links point to github.com, it references a specific issue number, and it asks for no credentials. The unsubscribe link is standard.
lesson: Automated notifications from services you use are legitimate when they link to the real domain and ask for nothing.

body: Your order #8847291055 is being prepared. Estimated delivery: 35 mins. Track: zomato.com/track/8847291055 . Rate after delivery to get Zomato Pro benefits.
explanation: A real order confirmation with a specific order number, a link to the official domain, and no request for payment or credentials. The tracking link is informational.
lesson: Order confirmations from services you just used are legitimate. Check that the link points to the real domain.

body: Beta, I transferred Rs 5000 to your account for the books you mentioned. Check and let me know. Mom says don't forget to call on Sunday.
explanation: A saved contact, a specific amount you discussed, and a family reminder. No link, no request for credentials, no urgency. The context is something you can verify by checking your bank app.
lesson: Messages from saved contacts about conversations you remember are almost always legitimate.

subject: Campus placement drive: Infosys, 25 November
body:
Dear final year students,

Infosys will be conducting a campus placement drive on 25 November 2024.

Eligibility: 60% throughout, no active backlogs
Registration: Submit your resume at the placement cell (Room 204, Admin Block) by 20 November.

Pre-placement talk: 24 November, 3 PM, Seminar Hall

For queries, visit the placement cell or email placement@yourcollege.ac.in

- Training & Placement Officer
explanation: This is a real placement announcement. It comes from the college's official domain, registration happens in person at a named room, and there's no fee or online form link. The contact information is the same email that sent it.
lesson: Legitimate placement drives require in-person registration and never charge fees. The contact method matches the sender.

body: Paytm: Rs 150 received from 98XXXXXX12. Balance: Rs 1248. If not you, call 0120-4456-456 or freeze in app. Never share OTP.
explanation: A real transaction alert with the official Paytm helpline, a directive to use the app, and an explicit warning not to share OTP. It asks for nothing and contains no link.
lesson: Genuine payment alerts warn you against sharing secrets and direct you to official channels.

body:
Hey everyone! TechFest 2024 registrations are now open.

Events: Hackathon, RoboWar, Quiz, Gaming
Dates: 15-17 December
Registration fee: Rs 200 per event (pay at the fest desk)

Registration desk: Student Activity Centre, 10 AM - 4 PM till 10 Dec

Queries: Call Arjun (98XXXXXX34) or visit the desk.

Let's make this the biggest fest yet! 🎉
explanation: This is from a saved contact (the fest committee), registration happens in person at a named location, payment is at the desk (not online), and there's a named person to call. No QR code, no link, no urgency.
lesson: College events you're involved in are legitimate when registration and payment happen in person at known locations.

subject: Your weekly digest from Medium
body:
Hi Priya,

Here are this week's top stories based on your reading history:

1. "Understanding React Hooks" by Dan Abramov
2. "The Future of AI in Education" by Andrew Ng
3. "Clean Code Principles" by Robert Martin

Read on Medium: https://medium.com

You're receiving this because you subscribed to the weekly digest.
Unsubscribe: https://medium.com/me/settings
explanation: A newsletter you subscribed to, with links to the real medium.com domain. It asks for no credentials and provides an unsubscribe link. The content matches your interests.
lesson: Newsletters you remember subscribing to are legitimate when they link to the real domain and ask for nothing.

subject: Guest lecture: Machine Learning in Healthcare
body:
GUEST LECTURE

Topic: Machine Learning Applications in Healthcare
Speaker: Dr. Priya Sharma, AIIMS Delhi
Date: 28 November 2024, 2:00 PM
Venue: Seminar Hall, CS Department

All students are invited. Attendance will be marked.
Certificate of participation will be provided.

- Head of Department
Computer Science
explanation: A real academic event announcement. It happens at a named venue on campus, attendance is marked (so you can verify by showing up), and there's no registration fee or online form. The speaker is from a real institution.
lesson: Academic events announced on department notice boards are legitimate when they happen on campus with no fee.

body: Swiggy: Your order from Domino's is on the way! Rider: Rahul (98XXXXXX56). Track live: swiggy.com/track . Enjoy your meal!
explanation: A real delivery update with the rider's name and a masked phone number, a link to the official domain, and no request for payment or credentials.
lesson: Delivery updates from services you just ordered from are legitimate when they link to the real domain.

body:
Amit: Guys, the OS exam is postponed to 5 Dec
Priya: Really? Prof said it was on 28th
Amit: Yes, he announced in the other section today. Check the portal, it's updated
You: Thanks Amit, I'll verify on the portal
Rahul: Confirmed, portal shows 5 Dec now
explanation: A group conversation where someone shares news, others verify it independently through the official portal, and the information is confirmed. No link, no urgency, just normal student coordination.
lesson: When information is verified through an independent official source (the portal), it's legitimate.

subject: Your certificate for "Machine Learning" is ready
body:
Hi Priya,

Congratulations! You've successfully completed the course "Machine Learning" by Stanford University.

Your certificate is now available:
https://www.coursera.org/account/accomplishments/verify/ABC123XYZ

You can also download it from your profile.

Keep learning!
The Coursera Team
explanation: This is a real certificate notification from a course you completed. The link points to coursera.org, it includes a specific verification code, and it asks for no credentials. The congratulations are appropriate for a completed course.
lesson: Completion notifications from courses you finished are legitimate when they link to the real domain and include specific details.

subject: Library timing change during exams
body:
NOTICE

Library Timing During Semester Exams
(1 December - 20 December)

Extended Hours: 8 AM to 11 PM (Mon-Sat)
Sunday: 9 AM to 8 PM

ID card mandatory for entry
Silent zone will be strictly enforced

For queries, contact the librarian (Room 3, Ground Floor)

- Chief Librarian
explanation: A real administrative notice about timing changes. It's posted at the library entrance (where you'd expect it), gives specific dates and times, and directs queries to a physical location. No QR code, no link, no fee.
lesson: Administrative notices posted at the relevant location about operational changes are legitimate.
